newsitem.title: USA: Duff may raise Houston Industries, NorAm ratings.
newsitem.headline: Duff may raise Houston Industries, NorAm ratings.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said on Tuesday it may raise the debt ratings of Houston Industries Inc and NorAm Energy Corp.
This follows a review of Houston Industries' proposed $3.9 billion acquisition of NorAm.
Duff said it put Houston Industries on "rating watch-up" for a possible increase, changing its status from "rating watch-down," which indicated a possible cut in rating.
It put NorAm Energy and NorAm Financing I on "rating watch-up." Previously, it said the rating action was uncertain.
Duff said it may cut the ratings on Houston Lighting & Power Co, which remains on "rating watch-down." Houston Lighting is a unit of Houston Industries.
Duff said its preliminary post-merger estimates for Houston Industries are single-A-minus for unsecured notes and senior debentures and D-One for commercial paper.

Preliminary ratings for Houston Lighting are first mortgage bonds, secured medium-term notes and collateralized pollution control revenue bonds at single-A; noncollateralized pollution control revenue bonds at single-A-minus; preferred stock triple-B-plus, and commercial paper at D-One.
Duff said NorAm's post-merger credit ratings are expected to be: notes and debentures triple-B, and convertible preferred stock and trust originated preferred securities triple-B-minus.

DCR currently rates Houston Industries' unsecured notes and senior debentures triple-B-plus and commercial paper D-Two. Houston Lighting's first mortgage bonds, secured medium-term notes and collateralized pollution control revenue bonds are rated single-A-plus; noncollateralized pollution control revenue bonds and preferred stock single-A, and commercial paper D-One.

NorAm's unsecured notes and debentures, which were upgraded in May, are rated triple-B-minus; convertible exchangeable preferred stock double-B-plus, and NorAm Financing I's trust originated preferred securities double-B-plus.
